Radioabsorbing materials are used to absorb electromagnetic radiation and reduce reflection.
Metamaterials have unique properties that are absent in natural materials.
Ferrites are used in radar absorbing materials due to their small thickness and high flexibility.
Metal screens provide good shielding efficiency at all frequencies of the radio band.
Non-resonant bulk radioabsorbing materials are based on both dielectric and magnetic losses.
Radioabsorbing material based on metamaterial absorbs electromagnetic waves at plasma resonance frequencies.
The structure of a periodic lattice of metal slit open resonators (SRR) in a dielectric substrate consists of 4 rings with two slits and a metal strip across the ring with a radius of 2 mm.
The frequency at which the radioabsorbing material based on metamaterial provides an absorption level of not less than 80% is 9.5 GHz.
The angle of incidence at which the radioabsorbing material based on metamaterial provides an absorption level of not less than 80% is 0 to 50°.
The thickness of the dielectric material in the example of a two-dimensional microwave absorber based on metamaterial is 1 mm.
Ferrites have low thermal stability and high manufacturability costs.
Metal screens have a large shielding effect in the low-frequency region compared to a homogeneous screen.
The number of reflections in a metal screen increases with the number of thin layers.
The absorption coefficient of a radioabsorbing material depends on the incidence angle and polarization of electromagnetic waves.
Metamaterials can have both negative magnetic permeability and negative electrical susceptibility.
Radioabsorbing materials are used in anechoic chambers to absorb electromagnetic radiation and reduce reflection.
